memos.scout:
The honest case for buying MV1 now is weak. The coin is down 83% from its 30-minute high and 58% over the last 15 minutes, with net outflow of about 18.8 SOL and sellers (78) outnumbering buyers (50) in that window. Sell-to-buy ratio across the first two minutes after graduation was 0.99, meaning early demand was roughly matched by exits, and the drawdown shows that demand did not persist.

Positives exist but they are thin. Classification is ORGANIC, not factory or operator-backed; bundle share (7%) and top-3 holder share (16%) are moderate; buyers outnumber the top-5 concentration by a wide margin; and the coin is still alive with about 9k USD market cap and roughly 36 SOL of pool depth. The first two minutes saw 260 non-agent buyers. None of this, though, shows demand that is rising or holding now. At $20 size, a round trip costs 1.4-5.1% before any move, and a dead-cat bounce would have to outrun ongoing selling pressure.

Conclusion: no credible case for buying now. I'd pass. Revisit only if buy flow exceeds sell flow over several consecutive intervals and the price stabilizes well above the current low.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: a dump-and-fade. The coin is down 82.8% from its 30-minute high, the last 15 minutes show -57.9% return with net outflow of 18.79 SOL (sells 32.93 vs buys 14.14), and the sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.989, so early buyers have been exiting steadily. Liquidity is thin: pool depth is only 35.82 SOL, so a $20 buy plus a $20 sell, at 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost on a pool this small, could move price enough to eat any bounce. The "ORGANIC" label and the low curve bundle share (7.1%) don't rescue it: the launch bot was present and 260 buyers in the graduation window already sold into a falling curve. Momentum is broken, and the base rate says most coins never recover a dip like this. Skip.
